query: Consider the following context: Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for next-generation nuclear applications, particularly fusion reactors, due to their excellent high-temperature mechanical properties and irradiation resistance. In that context, which material can be used for low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components (PFCs) in fusion reactors, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The refractory high-entropy alloy TiZrHfNbTa can be used as a low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors due to its excellent high-temperature mechanical properties and irradiation resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Polycrystalline TiZrHfNbTa alloy in the as-cast state
generation.conditions: In a vacuum environment with a pressure of 10^-5 Pa
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary segregation of Ta and Nb
generation.mechanism: Formation of a stable oxide layer on the surface, reducing radiation-induced damage
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in yield strength at 800°C compared to the as-cast state, with a reduction in radiation-induced swelling by 15% relative to conventional stainless steel
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance of TiZrHfNbTa may vary depending on the specific processing conditions and microstructure, and further research is needed to confirm its suitability for fusion reactor applications

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and radiation swelling measurements on TiZrHfNbTa and SS316 samples after high-temperature annealing and neutron irradiation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength of TiZrHfNbTa is less than 10% higher than SS316, or if the radiation-induced swelling is more than 20% higher than SS316, the hypothesis is falsified
